question: What steps must I follow to resolve a roommate conflict before a room change can be approved?
answer: To resolve a roommate conflict, you must start by speaking directly with your roommate or floor mate. If that does not work, you must speak with your Resident Assistant (RA) to facilitate mediation. If a resolution is still not reached, you must then speak with your Residence Life Coordinator (RLC). If the situation remains unresolved, a room change may be possible if space is available.
quote: For roommate or ﬂoor mate conﬂicts, the process begins by speaking with your roommate or ﬂoor mate. If it cannot be worked out, you must then speak with your Resident Assistant (RA) to facilitate mediation. If resolution is still not made, then you are to speak with your Residence Life Coordinator (RLC).

question: What are the quiet hours on weekdays and weekends, and how do they change during finals?
answer: Quiet hours are from 10:00 pm to 8:00 am from Sunday through Thursday, and from 12:00 am to 10:00 am on Friday and Saturday. During finals week, 24-hour quiet hours are enforced starting the day before the first day of finals.
quote: Quiet Hours: ● Sunday-Thursday 10:00 pm-8:00 am ● Friday & Saturday 12:00 am-10:00 am ● During Finals week there are 24-hour quiet hours that are enforced starting on the day before the ﬁrst day of Finals

question: How long can an overnight guest stay, and whose permission or notification is required?
answer: An overnight guest is permitted to stay for up to three consecutive nights. The host is required to get permission from their roommate, obtain a guest pass from Security, and notify their RA.
quote: Residents may have overnight guests for up to three (3) consecutive nights. As host, you need permission from your roommate, and a guest pass from Security. You also need to notify your RA.

question: Which students must live in college housing and have a dining plan, and what exceptions are listed?
answer: Full-time students must live in College housing and subscribe to a dining plan during their first six credit terms. The exceptions to this policy include married students, military veterans with two years of active duty, students with dependent children, and commuting students who live with their parents or legal guardians within a 30-minute commute.
quote: For this reason, full-time students are required to live in College housing and subscribe to a dining plan during their ﬁrst six credit terms. College housing includes residence halls, fraternities, sororities, apartments, special interest houses, and townhouses. Exceptions to this policy include married students, military veterans with two years of active duty, students with dependent children, and commuting students who live with their parents/legal guardians within a 30-minute commute.

question: I locked myself out at 11 p.m. on Saturday. Who should I contact, and would that be different during weekday office hours?
answer: If you lock yourself out at 11 p.m. on Saturday (which is on the weekend), you should contact Security to let you in. This is different from weekday office hours (a college work day), during which you should call the Residence Life Office.
quote: In the event a student is locked out of their room during a college work day, the student should call the Residence Life Oﬃce (608-363-2350). If it is after oﬃce hours or on the weekend, the student should contact Security, who can let them in.

question: I lost my room key. What steps do I need to take to get a replacement?
answer: If you lose your room key, you must contact Residence Life immediately, complete a key replacement form, and bring that form to Security so they can cut a new key for you.
quote: If the student loses their key, they should contact Residence Life immediately, ﬁll out a key replacement form, and take it to Security to have a new key cut for their room.

question: What should I do if I lose my student ID, and is the first replacement free?
answer: If you lose your student ID, you should report it to Residence Life and fill out a lost ID card form. The first replacement card is provided for free.
quote: Students who have lost their ID card/meal card/key card should report it to Residence Life and ﬁll out a lost ID card form. Residence Life will make you a new card for free if it is your ﬁrst time losing it.

question: I paid the guest meal price because I forgot my ID. Can I get a refund?
answer: Yes, you can receive a full refund if you present the receipt and your valid ID at the Food Service Oﬁce within 72 hours.
quote: However, the student will be issued a receipt and can receive a refund, in full, if the student presents the receipt and their valid ID at the Food Service Oﬁce within 72 hours.

question: What must I do before parking in a campus Student Parking lot, and what happens if I leave a parking ticket unpaid for more than 30 days?
answer: To park in designated Student Parking areas, you must purchase a parking permit. If you do not pay a parking ticket within 30 days, the fine will double and the charge will be added to your student account.
quote: After 30 days, the ﬁne will double and the charge will be added to the student account.

question: I am already living on campus for summer housing or an activity. When must I clear an Accounting/Enrollment hold, and what happens if I do not?
answer: You must clear the Accounting/Enrollment hold at least one week before the first day of classes. If you do not meet this deadline, you will be required to move out of the Residence Halls and will not be allowed to attend classes or participate in co-curricular activities.
quote: Students who are already living in the Residence Halls due to summer housing or co-curricular activities must clear an Accounting/Enrollment hold no later than one week before the first day of classes. Students who do not meet this deadline will be required to move out of the Residence Halls and may not attend classes or participate in co-curricular activities.

question: I earned a D+ in a course. Can I repeat it, and which attempt counts toward my GPA and earned units?
answer: Yes, you can repeat the course because you received a grade of “D+” or lower. The credit from your most recent course attempt will be used to calculate your grade point average and earned unit count.
quote: Students may repeat a course if they received a grade of “D+” or lower. Credit for the grade from the most recent course attempt will be used in calculating the grade point average and earned unit count.

question: Under what circumstances can I receive an incomplete grade?
answer: Incomplete grades are granted only in cases of serious illness or injury, family crisis, or another substantiated unforeseen circumstance beyond the student's control that prevents them from completing all course requirements by the end of the semester.
quote: Incomplete grades shall be granted only in cases of serious illness or injury, family crisis, or some other substantiated unforeseen circumstance beyond the control of the student that would make it impossible to complete all course requirements by the end of the semester.

question: How do I drop a course after the first week of classes but before the drop deadline?
answer: To drop a course after the first week of classes and before the relevant drop deadline, a student must acquire an Add/Drop Card from the Registrar’s Office located on the second floor of Pearsons Hall. This card must be completed with the drop details and the written approval of the course instructor(s) and the primary academic advisor (AMP or Major), and then returned to the Registrar’s Office for final processing.
quote: A student can drop a course after the first week of classes and before the relevant drop deadline by acquiring an Add/Drop Card from the Registrar’s Office on the second floor of Pearsons Hall.

question: How many earned units do I need to graduate, and what minimum GPA is required overall and in my major?
How many units can a Data Science or Data Analytics major double-count toward another major or minor?
answer: If a student majoring in data science or data analytics wishes to major or minor in another discipline, they are allowed to double-count up to four units.
quote: If students majoring in data science or data analytics want to major or minor in another discipline, up to four units are allowed to be double counted.

question: Can AP credit satisfy the writing or quantitative reasoning requirements, and how does that differ from transferring a college course?
answer: AP credits cannot be used to satisfy writing or quantitative reasoning requirements. In contrast, a transferred college course can be used to fulfill the quantitative reasoning requirement and up to one of the three required writing courses.
quote: AP/IB/GCE A-level credits may not be used to fulfill any of these requirements.

question: I want to take a course at another college to meet Beloit's quantitative reasoning requirement. What should I do before enrolling, and what minimum grade would make it eligible for transfer?
answer: Before enrolling in a course at another institution, you should complete the Transfer Credit Authorization Form. To be eligible for transfer, you must earn a grade of "C" or better in the course.
quote: Students enrolled at Beloit who wish to transfer credits for coursework taken after matriculation should complete the Transfer Credit Authorization Form prior to enrolling in a course elsewhere.

question: I missed the normal drop deadline but am still earning a D. Can I request a WP, what documentation is needed, and will I receive credit?
answer: Yes, you can request a "withdraw passing (WP)" if you are earning a D grade. To do so, you must provide a written petition (including the course number, section, title, semester, and instructor name), have your instructor provide a written statement verifying that you were passing the course with a "D" or better grade at the time of the request, and have your advisor provide a written statement. No credit is granted for a course in which a WP is received.
quote: A student must - provide a written petition requesting a “WP” (including the course number/section/title, the semester, and instructor name). - have the instructor provide a written statement verifying that the student was passing the course with a “D” or better grade at the time of the request. - have their advisor provide a written statement.

Can I bring a pet cat to campus housing, and would calling it an emotional support animal be enough?
answer: No, simply calling a cat an emotional support animal is not enough. You must receive official Emotional Support Animal designation from the Director of Learning Enrichment and Disability Services prior to bringing the animal to campus. Without this authorization, the animal cannot be kept on campus.
quote: Students must receive Emotional Support Animal designation from the Director of Learning Enrichment and Disability Services (hereto referred to as “Director”) prior to bringing their animal to campus. Without such authorization, an animal cannot be kept on campus.
